documents.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI

source.lean_scope: The reader shows the authors’ source at their published revision. Compiled dependency and axiom metadata is available for six declarations.

about.heading: Verification
paragraphs: The authors report that Lean Comparator accepted the six challenges. The reader also has independent replay evidence for the fixed-point arcsin and Find-Any challenges.

links.label: Frozen challenge statements and independent replay outcomes

topics.name: Quantum Hoare logic and formal verification
topics.description: The authors specify quantum programs with classical control in Lean. They use Hoare triples to state correctness and give separate rules for resource costs. Lean Comparator checks candidate proofs against the frozen specifications.

topics.name: Parallel Grover search
topics.description: In a domain of size $N=2^n$, Find-Any returns one marked index and Find-All returns the whole marked set. Lean proves both guarantees with probability one. For all 121 combinations of query limit $m$ and marked count $k$, Lean also bounds the expected rounds averaged over marked sets, for sufficiently large $N$. For large domains, Find-Any uses weak measurements. Some Find-All settings use a quantum walk over subsets of the domain.

topics.name: Reversible fixed-point arcsin
topics.description: The circuit approximates $\arcsin(y)$ on a signed 25-bit grid and adds its code to the output register modulo $2^{25}$. It preserves the input and returns the ancillas to zero. The Lean theorems give a uniform absolute error of at most $1.25\times10^{-7}$ on the grid in $[-1,1]$ and a spacetime cost of at most $369{,}800$.

topics.name: Stopping power in inertial-confinement fusion
topics.description: Stopping power is the mean kinetic energy a projectile loses per unit distance traveled. The benchmark simulates an $\alpha$ particle and 218 electrons moving among 216 fixed protons. For each of ten evolution times the compiled circuit approximates $e^{-iHt}$ to error $10^{-2}$ on grid states antisymmetric under exchange of same-spin electrons. Lean bounds the logical qubit count times the sum of the $T$-gate bounds for the 500 evolutions.

topics.name: Non-Born–Oppenheimer dynamics of C₂₃H₂₀N₃O
topics.description: The circuit approximates one femtosecond of time evolution for C₂₃H₂₀N₃O on a grid with quantum nuclei and electrons. Lean bounds the error on every system input with zero ancillas and the product of the logical qubit count and T count.

topics.name: Cytochrome P450 Compound I
topics.description: The authors compile a phase-estimation circuit for the fixed Hamiltonian of Compound I in active space X. Lean bounds the capped root-mean-square energy error by 1 mHa on the 63-electron sector and the cost by 436,509,499,221 qubit–T. The adjusted baseline in Appendix I.2 is about 2.49 times that cost bound.

reader.link_caveat: The authors’ reported verification and the reader’s editorial comparisons are separate evidence.
